evals.name: braille-fetch-indicator
evals.prompt: I have a plain static HTML page at index.html in this directory. When the Search button is clicked it fetches results from the npm registry — please add a loading indicator that shows while the fetch is in flight and disappears when results arrive. I'd like one of those terminal-style braille spinners like CLI tools show. No frameworks, no build step, just edit the file.
evals.expected_output: index.html modified with a braille-frame spinner (⣾⣽⣻⢿⡿⣟⣯⣷ or similar) driven by setInterval, shown during fetch, hidden after, with role=status and reduced-motion handling
assertions: Braille spinner frames (⣾⣽⣻-style or ⠋⠙⠹-style glyphs) are cycled via JS interval
Indicator is shown when the fetch starts and hidden when results arrive (including on error path or via finally)
The spinner interval is cleared when loading finishes — no leaked timer
Indicator has accessible status markup (role=status or aria-live/aria-label)
Original search behavior intact: form submit still fetches npm registry and renders results list
Monospace font used for the glyph so frames don't jitter horizontally

evals.name: jinja-dots-form
evals.prompt: upload.html in this directory is a Jinja2 template from my Flask app. The form POST can take ~10 seconds for big CSV files — show an animated bouncing-dots loader next to the Upload button while the request is pending, and disable the button so people don't double-submit. Plain CSS/JS only, no build step, no libraries.
evals.expected_output: upload.html modified with a three-dot bouncing loader (staggered CSS keyframes), revealed on form submit, button disabled, valid Jinja preserved
assertions: Loader is three (or more) dots animated with staggered CSS keyframes (per-dot animation-delay)
Loader hidden initially and revealed on form submit
Submit button gets disabled on submit to prevent double-submission
Jinja structure preserved: extends, block content, url_for, and error conditional all intact
Form submission is not prevented — the POST still goes through natively (no preventDefault without a manual submit)
Loader has accessible status markup (role=status or aria attributes)
prefers-reduced-motion is respected (animation replaced or calmed under the media query)

evals.name: morph-standalone
evals.prompt: Give me a standalone HTML snippet of a loading animation where a filled shape morphs between circle, square, triangle and so on — around 48px, in my brand color #6d28d9. It has to be fully self-contained (markup + styles in one block) so I can paste it into my static site. Save it as morph-loader.html.
evals.expected_output: morph-loader.html: self-contained snippet, shape genuinely morphs (SMIL or CSS d/path animation), 48px sizing, #6d28d9 color, accessible root
assertions: The shape genuinely morphs between geometries (SMIL animate on path d, or CSS d:path()/clip-path interpolation) — not a crossfade, spin, or border-radius-only trick
At least circle, square, and triangle shapes appear in the sequence
Rendered size is approximately 48px
Brand color #6d28d9 is used for the shape
Fully self-contained: no external stylesheets, scripts, CDNs, or framework dependencies
Root element has accessible status markup (role=status + aria-label)
Each shape holds briefly before morphing to the next (not a continuous blur of motion)
